  "repair_strategy": "Add a blur event listener to the input field in the non-inline picker setup that calls the Datepicker instance's hide method. This ensures the calendar closes whenever the input loses focus, regardless of date validity. Using the Datepicker's hide method (which delegates to picker.hide and resets the view) is safer than calling picker.hide directly because it handles inline pickers gracefully and resets the view state.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "js/Datepicker.js",
      "sha256": "55bc634a806da095ca30921bdc0d463fdc2fd63dff3eeab32b3d673bab3ef609",
      "before": "      // set up event listeners in other modes
      const onMousedownDocument = onClickOutside.bind(null, this);
      const listeners = [
        [inputField, 'keydown', onKeydown.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'focus', onFocus.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'mousedown', onMousedown.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'click', onClickInput.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'paste', onPaste.bind(null, this)],
        [document, 'mousedown', onMousedownDocument],
        [document, 'touchstart', onMousedownDocument],

      ];
      registerListeners(this, listeners);",

        [document, 'touchstart', onMousedownDocument],
        [window, 'resize', picker.place.bind(picker)]
      ];
      registerListeners(this, listeners);"
    }
  ],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker will close, preventing focus trap and preserving logical tab order. The picker closes for both valid and invalid dates.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Mouse users clicking on the picker calendar will cause the input to lose focus (blur), triggering hide before the mousedown handler can process the click. This may close the picker prematurely and interfere with date selection by mouse. However, the existing click-outside handler uses capture-phase mousedown on document, which fires after blur; the picker may already be hidden.
